comparisons.peer_topic: CISO Role, Expertise, and Team Structure
comparisons.peer_summary: Citi's CISO, who reports to the Head of Technology and Business Enablement, manages material cybersecurity risks and is supported by a team of approximately 3,400 individuals including subject matter experts in various security domains.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and C disclose the specific role and reporting structure of their Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) as part of their governance framework. GS states that its CISO provides regular briefings to the Board on cybersecurity matters, while C identifies its CISO as having primary responsibility for assessing and managing material cybersecurity risks and reports to the Head of Technology and Business Enablement.

sentences.text: The Board also receives regular briefings from our CISO on a range of cybersecurity-related topics, including the status of our Cybersecurity Program, emerging cybersecurity threats, mitigation strategies and related regulatory engagements.

Citi's Head of Foundational Services and CISO, who reports directly to Citi's Head of Technology and Business Enablement, has primary responsibility to assess and manage Citi's material risks from cybersecurity threats.

comparisons.peer_topic: Board and Committee Oversight of Cybersecurity
comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm's Board of Directors receives periodic updates from the CIO, CISO, and senior CTOC members concerning cybersecurity matters, including developments, policies, initiatives, and significant incidents. The Audit Committee and Risk Committee assist the Board in this oversight, while the Global Technology Operating Committee (GTOC) governs the Firmwide Global Technology organization and resolves key operational risk matters.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and JPM describe the Board receiving periodic updates from the CISO and other senior technology executives regarding cybersecurity matters. GS notes the Board receives regular briefings from the CISO on program status and threats, while JPM's Board receives periodic updates from the CISO and CIO concerning cybersecurity developments and policies.

sentences.text: The Board also receives regular briefings from our CISO on a range of cybersecurity-related topics, including the status of our Cybersecurity Program, emerging cybersecurity threats, mitigation strategies and related regulatory engagements.

As part of its oversight of management's implementation and maintenance of the Firm's risk management framework, the Firm's Board of Directors receives periodic updates from the CIO, the CISO and senior members of the CTOC concerning cybersecurity matters.

comparisons.peer_topic: Board of Directors and BOTC Oversight of Cybersecurity
comparisons.peer_summary: The Board of Directors oversees cybersecurity risks through the BOTC, which has primary responsibility for monitoring significant operational risk exposures including IT and cybersecurity. The BOTC receives quarterly reports from Technology, Operations, and NFR, reviews significant policies, obtains annual independent assessments, and facilitates direct discussion between senior management and Board members.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and MS detail Board-level oversight of cybersecurity risks through specific committees. GS specifies oversight by the Risk Committee and Technology Risk Subcommittee, whereas MS assigns primary responsibility for monitoring significant operational risk exposures, including cybersecurity, to the Board of Directors' Technology Committee (BOTC).

sentences.text: The Board, both directly and through its committees, including its Risk Committee and Technology Risk Subcommittee, oversees our risk management policies and practices, including cybersecurity risks, and information security and cybersecurity matters.

The BOTC has primary responsibility for assisting the Board in its oversight of significant operational risk exposures of the Firm and its business units, including IT, information security, fraud, third-party oversight, business disruption and resilience, and cybersecurity risks (including review of cybersecurity risks against established risk management methodologies) and the steps management has taken to monitor and control such exposures.
